description: create a second non-admin test user, dedicated to proving DATA-SECURITY-2.md finding #5's fix applies to @transaction's raw-SQL 'sql' opcode (scripting/authz.go's authorizeAndClassifySQL) too, not just the top-level @sql endpoint (sql_permissions.go's authorizeStatement) that sql-15/sql-16 above already cover. @transaction's route itself has no ego.sql requirement (routes.go gates it with Authentication(true) only), but its per-opcode Handler still requires ego.sql specifically to run the raw-SQL 'sql' opcode (handler.go's own comment: without that check, a baseline ego.logon-only caller could run arbitrary SQL through a transaction script that @sql itself would refuse outright) -- so this user needs ego.sql too, plus the same DSN- and table-level grants squ{{SQLTESTID}} needed.
